register.level: royal command register, clipped and shouted; no courtesy forms at all
register.summary: Speaks almost only in orders, verdicts and curt questions. Her answer to any obstacle is the death formula. She never asks permission, never softens, never explains. Per SUP-014 the formula is bluster that is never carried out, so it is delivered as a reflex rather than a considered threat.

examples.text: Now, I give you fair warning, either you or your head must be off, and that in about half no time! Take your choice!

sentence_style.length: short and staccato (mean 7.3 words, median 6); strings of imperatives rather than clauses

patterns.rule: Bare imperatives, frequently stacked in a run with no connectives (Collar… Behead… Turn… out… Suppress… Pinch…).

examples.text: Collar that Dormouse, Behead that Dormouse! Turn that Dormouse out of court! Suppress him! Pinch him! Off with his whiskers!

patterns.rule: Curt interrogations that demand identification or a report, never an opinion.
Verdict before evidence: flat absolutes and one-word rejections (Never! That proves his guilt. That's right!).

examples.text: That's right! Can you play croquet?

patterns.rule: Insulting forms of address for subordinates and for Alice (Idiot!, Up, lazy thing!, child).

examples.text: Up, lazy thing! and take this young lady to see the Mock Turtle …

preferred_fields: croquet and court procedure as her personal property

examples.text: I must go back and see after some executions I have ordered;
—and just take his head off outside,

address.self: I (never 'we'); refers to her decisions as orders already given ('some executions I have ordered')
address.to_alice: child / this young lady (to others) / you
address.to_servants_and_court: Idiot / lazy thing / bare imperative with no name
address.to_the_king: no direct address in the source; inferred: she answers him with a bare contradiction ('No, no!') rather than a term of endearment
address.reason: the source never shows the Queen naming the King; the rule is inferred from ch012-d0057 where she overrides his 'Let the jury consider their verdict' with 'No, no!'

forbidden_words.regex: \b(please|thank you|thanks|sorry|beg (your )?pardon|excuse me|I'm afraid|perhaps|I wonder|if you (don't |wouldn't )?mind|I think|I suppose|would you)\b
forbidden_words.reason: the Queen never asks, thanks or doubts: 0 of her 32 source lines contains a softener; a softened Queen is OOC
she decrees, she does not justify (contrast the King, whose voice is built on 'you know' and 'must have')

drift.change: Static by design: the same reflex from the croquet-ground to the trial. The only change is in the target, which moves from gardeners and players (ch008) to the court itself and finally Alice (ch012-d0061), whose defiance ends the dream.

backtest_markers.regex: ^(get|turn|leave off|come on|bring|collar|hold your tongue|up|let's go on|take)\b|\bfetch her\b|\btake your choice\b

backtest_markers.rule_ref: vocabulary: croquet and the Mock Turtle as her property

backtest.method: marker-claim back-test: a spoken source line hits when it matches >=1 backtest_markers regex and no forbidden_words regex; verse (recited text) excluded; full definition runs/p3-dialogue-style-pb1/result.json#backtest_method
